children.text: Nara states that she must let something simmer “for about five hours”, serving as a form of ragebait that is likely to garner engagement. With the first tag of her caption in this video being “#easyrecipe”, a process that involves a single step where something must simmer for five hours is completely contradictory. The comments on this video are filled with viewers calling Nara out for how long her recipes take, with many saying things like “dinner will be ready in 2 days” and “20 hour instant ramen”. This serves as a successful example of ragebait, where Nara’s choice was intentional and struck up more engagement on her video.

Throughout her cooking process, Nara can be seen wearing an elaborate outfit that she does not provide any context or commentary for. In a typical at-home cooking setting, high fashion is not fitting and serves no logical purpose. Nara’s choice to put on such an outfit while she works through a complicated recipe is an avenue to strike up engagement with the pure visual irony that it exudes. No viewer expects to see Nara wearing such an outfit while cooking in the comfort of her own home, so this serves as a popular point of engagement in the comment section. Users question the need for this level of fashion, ultimately uplifting the circulation of this video.
